title: CAVES Registry: International Registry for Chitosan-Associated Vasculitis with Eye and Sensorineural Symptoms (CAVES)
summary:
Background: To stop heavy bleeding after childbirth, doctors sometimes place a
material called chitosan into the womb. Chitosan is made from the shells of shellfish. In
a small number of women, a severe inflammation of the eyes and ears developed shortly
afterwards: the eyes became red, vision blurred, hearing declined, and there was
dizziness, ringing in the ears and painful swelling of the outer ear. If the symptoms are
recognised in time, they respond well to cortisone. If the condition goes unrecognised,
lasting damage to sight and hearing can remain. Only about 13 cases are known worldwide
so far.

Question: We want to find out how common this condition is, how it develops, which
treatment works best, and whether it can also occur after other operations in which
chitosan is used.

Methods: For this purpose we are setting up an international registry — a central
collection point to which hospitals in Germany and abroad can report their cases. Only
data that arise during normal treatment are used. No additional examinations, blood
samples or treatments take place. Data are passed on without names, so that the people
affected cannot be identified. Both earlier cases and newly occurring ones can be
reported. The registry is run at University Hospital Münster.

interventions.name: A new international registry for cases of CAVES syndrome (Chitosan-Associated Vasculitis with Eye and Sensorineural symptoms) is being established. It is coordinated at the Department of Ophthalmology, University Hospital Münster, Germany.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients treated with a chitosan-based product — in particular an intrauterine chitosan-based tamponade — following a surgical procedure, especially obstetric or gynaecological surgery
2. Development of acute inflammatory ocular disease (conjunctivitis, keratitis, scleritis, uveitis, retinal vasculitis) and/or acute inflammatory involvement of the vestibulo-auditory system within the first 14 days postoperatively
3. Written informed consent (for prospective cases), or fulfilment of the requirements for retrospective data collection
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pre-existing autoimmune uveitis or inner ear disease
2. Missing consent (for prospective cases)
